catalog_locator: Shimizu 1996: Preface sec. 4 'A linguistic summary'; Part One sec. 1.3 'Tones', items (21)-(23); Blench 2006: sec. 3.3 'Tones', p. 2.
catalog_quote: [Preface sec. 4] It has three distinct level tones, which are sometimes contracted to falling tones. [Part One 1.3 Tones] (21) There are three distinct tone levels, which can be demonstrated by many pairs of words.. kaana 111 go in!: kaana 221 V fry ... ηwan 2 V swallow: ηwan 1 V flay ε-naη 32 guts :ε-naη 11 root (22) Composite tones appear, though their nature is yet to be clarified: weyup 31[331?] ~yuyop 23 thick ... (23) Some sonorant consonants bear tone(s). So, non-initial nasals are all tone marked: jam 11. cal 32 woman [Blench 2006 sec. 3.3] Kulu has three level tones and at least two glide tones.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress
